# Policy And Exposure

This document covers inter-VLAN policy and service publication. The default posture is deny.

## Rule Baseline

1. Allow established and related traffic.
2. Drop invalid traffic.
3. Allow DHCP where required.
4. Allow DNS and NTP to the named infrastructure endpoints.
5. Allow management access from `VLAN 99`.
6. Allow named service flows only.
7. Apply VPN policy routing to `VLAN 50`.
8. Drop the rest.

## Zone Policy Summary

| Source | Destination | Action | Notes |
| ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| management | infrastructure and approved services | allow | Admin plane |
| management | internet | allow | Updates and diagnostics |
| server | internet | allow | Updates and backups |
| server | internal zones | deny by default | Reply traffic and named services only |
| lan | server | allow by service | Apps, storage, DNS |
| lan | iot | allow by service | Control paths and selective discovery only |
| lan | management, guest, work | deny by default | No lateral trust creep |
| iot | server | allow by service | DNS, NTP, MQTT, Home Assistant |
| iot | internet | allow by policy | Keep vendor access narrow |
| iot | management, lan, guest, work | deny by default | No lateral access |
| guest | internet | allow | Internet only |
| guest | any internal zone | deny | No exceptions |
| tv | server | allow by service | DNS, NTP, reverse proxy, media |
| tv | internet | allow via VPN | Forced egress path |
| tv | other internal zones | deny | Narrow on purpose |
| work | server | allow by service | Only named internal services |
| work | internet | allow | Standard outbound access |
| work | management, lan, iot, guest, tv | deny by default | Keep work separate |

## Named Service Flows

| Service | Host | Port | Allowed Sources |
| ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| DNS recursion | `server-dns-01.home.arpa` | `tcp/53`, `udp/53` | `management`, `server`, `lan`, `iot`, `tv` |
| AdGuard admin | `adguard.home.arpa` | `tcp/443` | `management`, `homelab-admins` |
| Home Assistant | `ha.home.arpa` | `tcp/8123` | `management`, `lan`, `iot`, `homelab-app-users`, `edge-proxy` |
| Reverse proxy | `proxy.home.arpa` | `tcp/443` | `management`, `lan`, `tv`, `work`, `homelab-app-users`, `edge-proxy` |
| NAS admin | `nas.home.arpa` | `tcp/443` | `management`, `lan`, `homelab-storage-users` |
| NAS file access | `server-nas-01.home.arpa` | `tcp/445` | `management`, `lan`, `homelab-storage-users` |
| MQTT | `mqtt.home.arpa` | `tcp/1883`, `tcp/8883` | `management`, `iot`, `lan` |
| Syslog | `server-log-01.home.arpa` | `udp/514`, `tcp/514` | `management`, `server` |
| Metrics UI | `server-monitor-01.home.arpa` | `tcp/443` | `management` |
| NTP | `mgmt-router-01.home.arpa` | `udp/123` | `management`, `server`, `lan`, `iot`, `tv`, `work` |
Guest has no internal services. Work gets no internal DNS overrides.

Remote NAS storage is tailnet-only. Do not expose `SMB` or other raw file protocols on the public edge.

Private tailnet-only app names use `*.tail.bigalan.dev`. Public app names use `*.bigalan.dev`. The same hostname is not reused for both roles.

## SSH Policy

- Linux edge and server nodes use Tailscale SSH as the primary admin path.
- `homelab-admins` SSH to the documented edge and server nodes over the tailnet.
- High-risk SSH users such as `root` use `check` mode.
- Public SSH stays closed on the documented Linux edge and server nodes.
- OpenSSH keys remain for break-glass access, bootstrap, and non-interactive service use.

Tailscale grants gate network access. Sensitive applications still keep their own authentication.

## TV VLAN VPN Policy

`VLAN 50` is forced through the VPN egress on the Flint 2. That policy is separate from Tailscale. Do not combine the TV VPN client with the Tailnet subnet router.

Allowed from `tv`:

- `server-dns-01.home.arpa` on `53`
- `mgmt-router-01.home.arpa` on `123`
- `proxy.home.arpa` on `443`
- approved local media endpoints behind the reverse proxy
- internet through the VPN path

Denied from `tv`:

- direct access to `management`
- direct access to `lan`
- direct access to `iot`
- direct access to `work`

## Discovery

- No blanket mDNS reflection.
- If casting or AirPlay needs reflection, add it as a named exception and document both source and destination zones.
- Do not reflect discovery into `guest`.
- Do not reflect discovery into `work`.

## Edge Zone

`edge` systems are external. They do not get broad access back into the homelab.

`edge-proxy-01.bigalan.dev` is the public reverse proxy for selected apps:

- It terminates `bigalan.dev` TLS publicly.
- It joins the tailnet as `tag:edge-proxy`.
- It reaches only the named app backends it publishes.
- It is managed over the tailnet with Tailscale SSH.
- It must not get blanket access to the `server` subnet.
- It must not publish `SMB`, `NFS`, router admin, switch admin, or AdGuard admin.

Other edge servers follow the same rule: join the tailnet for private admin and private service access, then expose public traffic only where a service is explicitly published.

Baseline published apps:

- `ha.bigalan.dev` -> `server-ha-01.home.arpa:8123`
- `media.bigalan.dev` -> `server-proxy-01.home.arpa:443`
